body.statement: There is a nonempty relatively open subset \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{abs}}\subset\mathcal G_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of the absorbed region on which \(\|\widetilde D\|_F/\sqrt{NT}\to a_D>0\), \(\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), and \(\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_F\}\to0\). Thus coverage is strictly below \(1-\alpha\) on \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{abs}}\), only for bounded \(h=\theta/\sigma\).
body.justification: A selected-factor bias of order \(m^{-1/2}\) dominates the conventional interval width of order \(m^{-1}\).
body.gap: Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) establish possible weak-factor distortion but not this explicit bounded-local low-rank-treatment zero-coverage region.
body.consumer: The result converts the absorption phase into a formal sensitivity failure for conventional whole-sample Wald inference within the oracle class.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(e_1,f_1\) be the treatment-support basis vectors in (2).  The strong-factor block calculation in (4)--(6), now evaluated at \(\widehat x_F\), shows that the first \(r\) selected left and right singular spaces converge to \(U_0\) and \(V_0\), while the additional selected singular pair is the leading pair of
\(Z_{22}+P_{\widehat x_F}\).  The absorption law and the separated argmin property give \(\widehat x_F\to x_\star\).  At a strictly subcritical point, the cited singular-vector theorem gives
\[
|\langle\widehat u,e_1\rangle|^2\xrightarrow{p}0,\qquad
|\langle\widehat v,f_1\rangle|^2\xrightarrow{p}0.              \tag{23}
\]
At a simple strictly supercritical point, take the singular-value decomposition of the two-by-two population spike.  The cited theorem, followed for \(c>1\) by the same transpose-and-rescale argument used in (8), gives
\[
|\langle\widehat u,e_1\rangle|^2
 \xrightarrow{p}\ell_c(s_\star)u_{\star,1}^2,\qquad
|\langle\widehat v,f_1\rangle|^2
 \xrightarrow{p}r_c(s_\star)v_{\star,1}^2.                    \tag{24}
\]
The projections on all distinct population spike directions vanish, which justifies the factors \(u_{\star,1}^2\) and \(v_{\star,1}^2\) in (24).  Strict separation from the edge and simplicity make (23)--(24) uniform on compact subsets of the stated regular set.

Since \(D=\sqrt{n_1t_1}\,e_1f_1^{\top}\), while \(e_1\perp U_0\) and \(f_1\perp V_0\),
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde D\|_F}{\sqrt{NT}}
=\sqrt{p_Nq_T}\,\|(I-P_{\widehat U})e_1\|_2
                   \|(I-P_{\widehat V})f_1\|_2.               \tag{25}
\]
Substitution of (23) or (24) into (25) proves the asserted formula for \(a_D\).  In the supercritical case, \(0<\ell_c(s)<1\) and \(0<r_c(s)<1\) for every finite \(s>c^{1/4}\); hence the two factors in braces are strictly positive even if a first singular-vector coordinate has absolute value one.  Compactness gives a common positive lower bound.

We next prove variance consistency rather than assuming it.  From the absorption law, \(\widehat\beta_F-\gamma=O_p(m^{-1/2})\).  Thus the nonbaseline signal in \(Y-\widehat\beta_FD\) has squared Frobenius norm \(O_p(T)\), because \(N/T\) is bounded above and below.  The matrix \(Y-\widehat\beta_FD\) differs from \(E\) by a matrix of rank at most \(r+2\).  Singular-value interlacing for a rank-\((r+2)\) perturbation bounds its residual sum of squares after deletion of \(r+1\) singular values between noise residual sums obtained by deleting fixed numbers of singular values, up to the preceding \(O_p(T)\) signal term and its Cauchy--Schwarz cross term.  The Gaussian law of large numbers gives
\[
\frac{\|E\|_F^2}{NT}\xrightarrow{p}\sigma^2,\qquad
\frac1{NT}\sum_{j=1}^{2r+3}s_j(E)^2=O_p(N^{-1})=o_p(1).         \tag{26}
\]
The signal contribution divided by \(NT\) is \(O_p(N^{-1})\), and its cross term divided by \(NT\) is \(O_p(N^{-1/2})\).  Hence
\[
\frac{\|Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2}{NT}
\xrightarrow{p}\sigma^2.                                     \tag{27}
\]
Because \(r\) is fixed and \(N/T\) stays in a compact subset of \((0,\infty)\), \(\nu_F/(NT)\to1\), so (27) proves \(\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\).

Finally set \(b(\eta,h)=x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b\).  On a compact subset of the stated absorbed set, \(|b|\) is bounded away from zero.  The absorption law gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}b(\eta,h),                                    \tag{28}
\]
whereas (25), (27), and \(NT\asymp m^2\) give
\[
\frac{\sqrt m}{\sigma}
\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F}{\|\widetilde D\|_F}
=O_p(m^{-1/2})\longrightarrow0.                               \tag{29}
\]
The event that the interval contains the target requires the absolute value of the left side of (28) to be no larger than (29).  Equations (28)--(29) therefore make its probability tend to zero, uniformly on compact subsets.  The small-radius certificate (22) also shows why nonemptiness of this regular absorbed set cannot follow from the frozen assumptions alone.
